title: SparseWeaver: Converting Sparse Operations as Dense Operations on GPUs for Graph Workloads
problem: Real-world graph workloads have sparse and skewed adjacency structures that cause severe warp-level load imbalance on GPUs, where existing software or hardware balancing schemes incur memory overhead or excessive inter- and intra-warp synchronization cost.
motivation: GPUs are the dominant platform for large-scale graph analytics, but irregular graph topology makes it nearly impossible to achieve efficient SIMT utilization without costly runtime rebalancing, limiting throughput.
method: SparseWeaver solves the problem of sparse graph operations causing GPU cores to sit idle unevenly by converting those operations into balanced dense operations that distribute work evenly. A lightweight hardware component called Weaver is added to GPU cores; it identifies patterns in the graph structure (using both compile-time and runtime analysis) where sparse operations can be converted to dense ones, then performs the conversion directly in the execution pipeline without extra memory overhead or synchronization delays. The design is tested on Vortex, an open-source RISC-V GPU.
key_novelty: A dedicated Weaver hardware unit converts sparse graph operations to dense operations by recognizing the underlying graph structure, eliminating memory and synchronization overhead compared to software approaches.
contributions: Analysis of common sparse operation patterns in GPU-based graph processing that enable dense conversion
Weaver: a lightweight functional unit microarchitecture for sparse-to-dense conversion exploiting memory locality
SparseWeaver hardware-software co-design framework that balances warp workloads for graph processing
2.36x speedup over state-of-the-art schemes with only 0.045% area overhead on RISC-V Vortex GPU
